thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Hosted inference p99 streaming latency spike detected for region-us-east-1. Affected service: /v1/streaming/generate. Triggered at 2026-03-15T14:10:21Z. Auto-page sent to oncall.
ada: saw the bot. p99 jumped from ~420ms to ~2.3s across multiple models. Lots of streaming stalls reported by logs.
sanjay: retasking paging — jordan oncall for infra today, cc @ken infra, @alyssa runtime.
jordan: oncall here, taking lead. can someone paste a quick top-level symptom summary? are requests queuing or GPU stalls?
ada: traces show long waits inside the accelerator layer before token emission. latency spike correlates with specific GPU nodes (gpu-node-7, gpu-node-12). KV cache hits are normal.
alyssa: streaming trace snippet: "token_emit_delay": 1900ms, backend exec time normal. Looks like scheduling / device stall rather than model slowness.
ken: I’m seeing machine metrics: gpu-node-7 shows repeated ECC correctable errors and temp spikes. nvidia-smi shows thermal throttle events.
ricardo: tagging in hw team. initial logs from node:

```
[GPU ECC] Correctable error count: 128
[GPU ECC] Last corrected at: 2026-03-15T14:08:55Z
[GPU THERMAL] Temp: 101C -> throttling engaged
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,ecc.errors.corrected --format=csv
GPU-0,101,65,128
```

ricardo: that error pattern + thermal throttling = flaky accelerator causing long tail latencies. could be fan/hw degradation or sudden load + cooling problem.
ada: customer impact: p99 SLO breached for streaming route in us-east-1. CS pinged with multiple customer complaints. We should consider immediate routing mitigation then live-mitigate node.
tess: customer-success: we're getting multiple support tickets. high-value customer A is seeing streaming stalls, they're asking for ETA. Please mark incident severity and give timeframe.
jordan: severity = sev-2 (customer-visible SLO breach across region). Immediate mitigations: 1) remove affected nodes from router pool, 2) warm-standby swap to other region/dedicated pool, 3) drain pods and failover. I'll coordinate.
nina: pre-check — can we drain node w/o massive cold-starts? we have warm-capacity in us-west-2 but scaling will add ~200ms to cold starts. advise downstream teams.
alyssa: quick routing policy change I can roll: set region routing weight us-east-1 -> 0.6, us-west-2 -> 0.4 for streaming, and enable forced fallback for in-progress streaming requests to compatible CPU fallback for high-timeout flows.

```json
{
  "route": "/v1/streaming/generate",
  "policy": {"fallback": "cpu-warm", "weights": {"us-east-1": 0.6, "us-west-2": 0.4}}
}
```

jordan: executing mitigation steps now. @ken start node quarantine & drain. @alyssa roll routing change. @nina notify CS with ETA.
ken: running drain command on gpu-node-7 and gpu-node-12

```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-7
kubectl drain gpu-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl label node gpu-node-7 redwood/quarantine=true
```

ken: drain in progress. some pods are rescheduling to us-west-2 via autoscaler.
ada: note: streaming sessions in-flight may still stall if they're mid-kv-cache ping to that device. alyssa, can we enable server-side reproxy to reattach clients to new instances?
alyssa: enabling streaming reproxy for affected sessions now. this should allow client reconnects without full cold-model loads for many flows.

(2m later)

jordan: routing change rolled. reproxy on. drains finishing. p99 reduced from 2.3s -> ~650ms but still above target.
ricardo: hardware note: gpu-node-7 fans show reduced RPMs -> possible hardware fan controller failure. scheduling swap of physical card or node replacement.
ken: while we arrange replacement, I'm moving traffic off entire rack to prevent recurrence. also enabling additional CPU fallback pool capacity.

```
# scale command
redwoodctl capacity scale --pool cpu-warm --replicas 40
```

tess: CS update sent to Customer A: "We're actively mitigating a regional GPU degradation causing streaming latency; we've rerouted and are working on hardware replacement. Estimated mitigation time 30-45m."
ada: monitoring dashboards: p95 back to 320ms, p99 ~580-700ms depending on model. still under investigation for residual tail events from remaining degraded nodes.
alyssa: found one model variant that hits larger KV cache sizes and suffers more from the stalls — we temporarily deprioritized that variant for live traffic.
jordan: handoff: I'll keep owning until hw swap completes. @ricardo please open hardware ticket with data and schedule node replacement. @nina please create incident ticket INC-2026-4321 and set postmortem owner.
ricardo: created HW ticket HW-7241, engineers assigned, ETA swap 2 hours due to spare GPU availability.
nina: INC-2026-4321 created. assigned to @jordan for follow-up. postmortem owner: ada.
ada: next steps: 1) monitor p99 for 2h, 2) collect full kernel logs and ECC event timeline, 3) vendor support run diagnostic, 4) change routing fallback to prefer dedicated pools for critical customers.
ken: one more mitigation: adding a short-term software rate limiter on bursty streaming connections from public tier to reduce thermal spikes.

```
# ingress limiter
rate-limit: 200 req/s per tenant
```

tess: CS: customers updated. we'll follow up with detailed incident note once postmortem ready.
jordan: for now, mitigation succeeded at reducing tail but still not fully resolved until hardware swap. I'm removing myself from active page list at 14:46 UTC, will monitor and be reachable. escalate to oncall if p99 > 1s again.
ada: thanks everyone. logging action items: hw swap (ricardo), postmortem (ada), incident ticket (nina), customer comms (tess), follow-up routing changes (alyssa/ken).
ricardo: adding vendor-ops debug notes to HW-7241: attach ECC dumps, thermal history, power cycle logs.
alyssa: will run evals on streaming variant set post-swap to validate regressions and rollback if needed.
nina: closing thread for now; will update incident doc with timeline and links. :white_check_mark:
